gen-fs-bevellier-gf-radio-canada: Cut-stencil cool, tightly spaced and graceful. Radio Canada follows in sans-serif, with tall, full c, s and z and a steady line that stays easy across a long passage.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-radio-canada-big: Bevellier's flat, stencil-cut strokes sit tight together, every glyph crowded close to its neighbors. And Radio Canada Big gives that a sans-serif counterweight, its big x-height and open terminals letting the text breathe.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-roboto: Roboto brings generous round mouths and a low step from capitals down to lowercase, a body that feels clean and current. Over a long stretch it reads smoothly, never fussy.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-ruda: Bevellier looks stencil-cut, graceful and tightly spaced. Ruda, a wire-thin sans-serif with a sizable x-height and wide-mouthed rounds, keeps a long passage approachable and clean on screen.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-saira: Bevellier draws wirelike strokes of one thickness, packed close with squat ascenders and a wide-looking lowercase. Saira answers with rounded letters stretching toward the top line and a visible gap in each s; body text probably wants a little extra size.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-savate: Bevellier's strokes never thin to hairlines, just flat, stencil-cut lines packed tight. Savate adds a restrained thick-and-thin rhythm and open curves, and that gentle difference is the strongest thing here.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Bevellier has a flat, stencil-cut look, single-weight strokes with no thick-thin modulation and very close spacing. But Schibsted Grotesk, a sans-serif with big open e and a and terminals that never close in, loosens everything up below.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-sen: Bevellier cuts flat, graceful letters from single-weight strokes with squat ascenders and tight spacing. Sen, a modern sans, does the quiet work instead: tall lowercase and constant-weight lines whose curves stop before turning inward.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-sintony: One thickness holds along each stroke, like a drawn cable. Sintony, a sans-serif with a chunky, tall midzone and curves that never clog, makes the strongest quality here a smooth, sturdy read beneath that graceful display.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-sofia-sans: Acrylic-stencil crisp, Sofia Sans stands tall with rounded letters, clearly open sides and no thick-and-thin modulation at all. Bevellier is better at graceful, close-set display; Sofia Sans is better at carrying the text.
